Article (plain text of the PDF):

Exact Certificates for the Proofreading Error Bound e−2∆ in All
Kinetic Networks with Two Bound States
Verifier-Gated Discovery Lab
Preprint, October 4, 2026

Abstract
Kinetic proofreading lets an enzyme discriminate a right substrate R from a wrong one
W beyond the equilibrium limit [1]. Scaling relations on the Pareto front have been studied
numerically [2]. A classification of the two-bound-state family with respect to the error bound
was not found in a literature search. At ∆ = ln 100 we prove for the linear Hopfield chain with
n = 2 that η ≥ e−3∆ for all positive rates and fuel potentials. Among the 88 non-degenerate
two-bound-state topologies, 50 provably obey η ≥ e−2∆ , 3 (fam2_66, fam2_9, fam2_11)
have exactly certified counterexamples with η < e−2∆ , and 35 remain open. Proofs use
symbolic positivity of polynomial coefficients. Counterexamples use exact rational rates. The
main limitation is that 35 topologies remain unclassified. The counterexamples are existence
statements within a bounded rate range.
Keywords: kinetic proofreading, error rate bound, Markov networks, entropy production,
exact certificates, Hopfield bound

1

Introduction

Hopfield showed that a strongly but nonspecifically driven reaction can raise specificity beyond
what free-energy differences or kinetic barriers allow [1]. The accuracy of error-correcting
pathways is set by the displacement of nucleoside triphosphates from equilibrium [3]. Several
checking steps can reach a given accuracy at lower dissipation than a single step [3]. In generalized
Hopfield models, more proofreading steps give better trade-offs among speed, error and dissipation
[2]. Scaling relations on the Pareto front were studied numerically [2]. Energy-relay proofreading
shows trade-offs and scaling laws [4] and a dynamical phase transition in the mixed regime
[4]. A kinetically controlled bound exists for proofreading networks [5, 6]. For a broad class of
networks, the ratio of speed, accuracy and entropy production stays asymptotically finite, while
scalings exist for Hopfield’s network where it diverges [7]. Excessive discrimination can remove
the nonequilibrium advantage [8], and a regime without accuracy gain exists [8].
Open question: is the chain bound η ≥ e−(n+1)∆ valid beyond the case n = 2 proved here?
For networks with two bound states, which topologies obey the bound e−2∆ and which can break
it?
Contribution: we give a symbolic proof of the chain bound for n = 2. We classify the
enumerated family of two-bound-state topologies into proved, refuted and open members. The
proved cases use symbolic positivity, the refuted cases exact rational certificates.
Summary of results.
• The chain-bound theorem shows η ≥ e−3∆ for hopfield_n2 for all rates and fuel potentials.
• The fam2_66 theorem certifies a counterexample to the two-bound-state bound.
• The proved-subfamily theorem and the consistency theorem prove the bound for 50 topologies.
1

 • The fam2_9/fam2_11 theorem certifies two further counterexamples.
• The classification theorem gives the split 50 / 3 / 35 of the 88 topologies.
• The supporting propositions give the family count, a partial proof, reachability certificates
for ten topologies and the verifier self-test.
• The examples give certified reachable points of hopfield_n1.

2

Model and assumptions

Notation. R is the right and W the wrong substrate, both traversing the same Markov network.
η = JW /JR is the error rate, v = JR the speed, and σ the entropy production per product in
units of kT . D = e∆ and G = eµ . Every edge has a reverse edge, local detailed balance holds,
and cycle affinities arise only from the fuel potential µ per activation and µP per product. These
are modelling rules of the verifier.
Fixed parameters:
• ∆ = ln 100, so e∆ = 100 and e−∆ = 0.01. W leaves bound states e∆ times faster than R.
• L = 10: every rate, including derived reverse rates, lies in [e−10 , e10 ].
• µ ≥ 0, explored in [0, 20]. µP ≥ 0, explored in [0, 20].
• max_states = 10: unbound states plus R and W copies of bound states.
• Substrate concentrations are absorbed into the binding rates (all equal to 1).
• Rates are rounded to rationals with denominator at most 106 for exact certificates.
• family_k = 2: the enumerated family has two bound states and 88 non-degenerate members.
For the chain with n proofreading stages, the Hopfield limits are 1e-4 for n = 1 and 1e-6 for
n = 2.

3

Method

Two certificate types are used.
• (a) Exact reachability. Rational rates in [e−10 , e10 ] satisfying local detailed balance are
checked in exact rational arithmetic. η is exactly rational, and σ is reported as an enclosing
interval.
• (b) Symbolic positivity. For a bound η ≥ B, the difference η − B is written as N/D in
the variables D = e∆ , G = eµ and the rates. The bound holds for all positive rates and
fuel potentials if all polynomial coefficients are nonnegative. This certificate is independent
of the rate range.
Interval enclosures of σ accompany type (a). Independent numerical re-computation is used
only as an adversarial cross-check (Appendix A).
The trusted base is the verifier code, which passes its self-test, and exact rational arithmetic.
Optimizer outputs, scans and fronts are numerical candidates until they pass a type (a) certificate.
A failed type (b) proof proves nothing; it leaves a topology open.
The work was carried out by an automated, verifier-gated laboratory in which every reported
statement was accepted only after passing code verification.

4

Results

4.1

Main results

Theorem 1 (Chain bound for n = 2). For hopfield_n2, η ≥ e−3∆ holds for all positive rates
and all fuel potentials µ, µP ≥ 0.

 Remark (status of computer-assisted parts). The chain-bound theorem, the provedsubfamily theorem and the consistency theorem are computer-assisted proofs whose trusted
base is symbolic expansion in exact rational arithmetic with a coefficient sign check. The
counterexample theorems, the reachability proposition and the examples are existence statements
checked in exact rational arithmetic at the stated rates. A third party re-runs everything with
the command in the Declarations. The classification theorem is the arithmetic combination of
these parts.

5

Negative results

Two questions yielded no verified claim. Their attempts and the reasons for failure (verifier
defects, later fixed, and one rate outside the allowed range) are listed in Appendix A.

6

Discussion, limitations and open questions

Within the family with two bound states, the bound e−2∆ holds for 50 of 88 topologies and fails
for fam2_66, fam2_9 and fam2_11, so it is not satisfied by every member. For the chain with
n = 2 the corresponding bound e−3∆ is proved for all rates.
Limitations. All results are for ∆ = ln 100. Counterexamples are existence statements with
rates in [e−10 , e10 ] and rational rounding. The σ and v values of the counterexample are those of
Table 2. Thirty-five topologies are open. Of the ten topologies in the reachability proposition,
only fam2_9 and fam2_11 are classified as counterexamples.
Open questions:
(i) Which of the open topologies obey η ≥ e−2∆ , and which can break it?
(ii) Do the remaining topologies of the reachability proposition admit η < e−2∆ strictly?
(iii) Does η ≥ e−(n+1)∆ hold for chains with n other than 2? Only n = 2 is proved here.
(iv) What structural feature of fam2_66, fam2_9 and fam2_11 explains the violation?

A

Agentic laboratory

Workflow. The laboratory ran 16 rounds with 14 verified statements and 2 negative results.
Every round was preregistered before the experiment. Preregistration H6 (commit 6184672) preceded the first run, and addenda are dated. The L2c success criterion (at least 5 counterexamples
in a round) was missed: 2 in round 12, 3 in total.
Agents and roles. The attempts recorded in the negative results involved the roles sparsam,
numeriker, skeptiker and theoretiker, run on the haiku and sonnet models, and a researcher role.
5

 Literature search. 2752 sources were retrieved (arXiv, Europe PMC, Crossref, citation
chain), 2502 screened, and 158 findings had a verbatim quote confirmed in the abstract by code.
All 11 classic-paper searches had a hit.
Red team. There were 29 counter-checks in total: 5 passed, 12 did not pass, 12 were not
executable. Selected outcomes:
• The parameters of the first example, with η = 3.650169e-04, σ in [6.000000, 6.000000] kT
and v = 1.0417e-01, remain admissible at a larger dissipation budget. The reported jump
of the front is therefore impossible, and the reported kink is an optimizer artifact.
• A symbolic attempt to prove a lower bound for hopfield_n1 failed, as expected.
• An independent verifier search for n = 2 (24 starts, seed 4711) found eta_min = 3.1387e-05
at sigma = 2665.585, v = 2.037e-06. It did not confirm the claimed value 1.0000e-07.
• Symbolic proofs of η ≥ 1/D2 failed for the members fam2_9, fam2_11 and fam2_13 (0 of
3 proved) and for 0 of 8 further members, consistent with their open status.
Additional certified statement (appendix only). For hopfield_n1 there exist rational
rates in [e−10 , e10 ] satisfying local detailed balance with η ≤ 0.0004, σ ≤ 8 kT per product and
v ≥ 0.001. Certificates (a): η = 3.156120e-04, σ in [6.000000, 6.000000] kT , v = 2.4255e-02; and
η = 2.043712e-04, σ in [3.079633, 3.079633] kT , v = 2.2592e-03. For 3 topologies, η ≥ 1/D2 was
also proved symbolically in a separate run.
Negative results in detail.
• Question: is a fuel-driven discard exit at the product state necessary to go below the
two-bound-state bound? No claim passed the verifier. All four attempts (roles sparsam,
numeriker, skeptiker, theoretiker; schranke_familie) failed because of a verifier defect, later
fixed.
• Question: do further open topologies reach η ≤ e−2∆ ? Certificate (a) passed for 10 of 11
cases. fam2_13 failed because a rate lay outside the allowed range [e−10 , e10 ] (derived
reverse rates included).
